Specify a conditional-logit matching model

Source: R/matching_model.R
matching_model.Rd

Specify conditional-logit model parameters for matching partners.

Usage

matching_model(formula, coefficients, group_exogamy = NULL, delta = NULL)

Arguments

formula

A one-sided R formula using age_difference and group predictors female_<group>, male_<group> and same_<group>. Use ~ 1 and numeric() coefficients for pair-effects-only matching.

coefficients

A finite named numeric vector of utility coefficients.

group_exogamy

Either a list or data.frame indicating the log odds of group exogamous pairings. See details for syntax.

delta

Optional male-target adjustments, as a named list keyed by dimension or a bare value for the only declared dimension: a finite numeric vector with unique category names.

Value

An inspectable hammel_matching_model list containing formula and coefficients.

Details

The formula argument can be used to define a formula for the utility \(U_{ij}\) of the match between woman i and man j. This utility is defined as the log of the unnormalized choice weight, such that the probability of woman i choosing man j is given by:

$$ P(j \mid i) = \frac{\exp(U_{ij})}{\sum_k \exp(U_{ik})} $$

where the denominator sums across all eligible male partners. This equation is equivalent to a conditional-logit model specification.

In practice, when groups are in use, this formula needs to be modified to adjust for expected male group shares, because the model uses women only to make the choice:

$$ P(j\mid i)= \frac{\omega_{g(j)}\exp(U_{ij})}{\sum_k\omega_{g(k)}\exp(U_{ik})} $$

where \(\omega_g\) is a group-specific weight to adjust for male group shares. More details are provided on the package website.

When delta = 0, the \(\omega\) weights will adjust male group shares to produce symmetry by gender in group exogamous unions. To allow for gender asymmetry, users can adjust delta values. The delta value will typically need to be tuned.

Users can define formulas based on:

  • age_difference: male age minus female age

  • female_<group>: group membership for <group> dimension of the woman.

  • male_<group>: group membership for <group> dimension of the man.

  • same_<group>: 0/1 numeric indicating same membership for man and woman.

Formula transformations such as I(age_difference^2) and abs(age_difference) are supported through stats::model.matrix(). If users limit the formula to age_difference and I(age_difference^2), utilities will be estimated in C++ leading to faster simulation runs.

Coefficient names must match the non-intercept model-matrix columns exactly, for example female_raceB. Names involving group predictors are checked when the model meets the group declaration at simulation. Supply all coefficients explicitly; no demographic coefficients are defaulted.

Users may find it easier to define group exogamy by the use of the group_exogamy argument than the use of a formula. This argument indicates the likelihood of group exogamy across multiple group dimensions. It can take one of two forms

  • List form: a named list keyed by dimension, such as list(race = c("A:B" = -2, "B:C" = NA), region = NA). Each value is a named vector over unordered pairs ("A:B" applies to female A/male B and female B/male A alike): a finite value is an additive log-weight effect and NA prohibits the pair; NA alone prohibits every union between different categories of the dimension. Effects from different dimensions add. Omitted pairs are treated as implicitly zero. Cross-dimension effects are not possible in this format.

  • Table form, for cross-dimension effects: a data frame with <group>_x and <group>_y columns for each dimension it uses and log_odds, such as data.frame(race_x = "W", region_x = "S", race_y = "B", region_y = "S", log_odds = -5). Each row is one unordered pair of category combinations, applied in both directions; NA prohibits it; unlisted pairs have an implicit log odds of zero.

Users may find age_gap_matching_model() more intuitive than specifying a direct formula.

Examples

# maximize age difference utility when husband is 5 years older. Double
# utility for same race unions
matching <- matching_model(
  ~ age_difference + I(age_difference^2) + same_race,
  c(
    age_difference = 0.1,
    "I(age_difference^2)" = -0.02,
    same_race = 0.69
  )
)
